transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is that I’ve gotten stuck doing these... little routines lately. 

Like washing my hands again after handling my wrist brace, or rechecking the stove and the front door. I also find myself silently counting through steps before I leave the house. It's just getting frustrating because they’re starting to make me late, even when I know perfectly well I’ve already checked everything and done enough.
Before you do these routines, do you get unwanted thoughts or urges that keep intruding into your mind?

Yes, I do. I’ll just be sitting and reading at home, or getting ready for my volunteer shift at the museum, and... well, an ugly little thought just keeps barging in. 

It's usually this nagging idea that I’ve left something unsafe, or touched something unclean, or that I've somehow put someone at risk. I know perfectly well that it’s out of proportion, but the thoughts just push their way in anyway, and they don't really settle down until I go do one of those routines.
When you do these routines, is it mainly to relieve the intrusive thought or to stop something bad from happening?

I suppose it's really to get relief from the thought itself. 

Like I mentioned a minute ago with those routines—washing my hands again after I adjust my wrist brace, or going back to recheck the stove and the front door. I guess part of me is trying to stop a fire or something bad from happening, but honestly, I mostly just do it to make that nagging feeling go away. If I just do my silent counting before I leave, the thought finally quiets down. 

It's just very frustrating because, as I said, I know perfectly well I've already done enough to be safe. But I still go through the motions just to clear my head, and then I end up running late.
Do you ever find yourself doing these routines even when there isn’t an intrusive thought bothering you first?

No, I don't think I do. It really seems to be the thought that starts the whole process. If I don't have that sudden worry about the stove or my hands, I don't feel any need to do the checking or the counting. It always seems to start with that nagging idea first.
